$comment: The source of sf-accordion's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/accordion (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

items.x-markup: the attribute takes the same list as JSON; without it the <details> written inside are the sections
items.summary: The sections, [{id, title, content | slot, open?, disabled?, icon?, badge?}]: an array in the property, the same array as JSON in the attribute. Without items the element takes the <details> written inside it.

single.summary: One section open at a time: opening one closes the one that was open.

size.summary: A step of the control ladder: the header is exactly the control height of the step, the height of an sf-input and an sf-button of the same size. Without it the roomy header of a content page.

appearance.summary: default: a filled surface; outline: a hairline border, no fill; flush: no fill and no radius, sections divided by a line, for panels and lists.

marker.summary: What marks a section open or closed: the chevron, or plus and minus.

single-section.summary: One section is a plain section -- its content shown, its heading not a toggle; toggle keeps it a disclosure, for a list that fills in later.

heading-level.summary: The level of each section's heading (role heading, aria-level).

expanded.summary: the ids of the open sections, in order

open.summary: Open the section with this id; in single mode the open one closes. sf-accordion:toggle fires for each section that changed, source method. Returns whether anything changed.

close.summary: Close the section with this id. Returns whether anything changed.

toggle.summary: Open the section if it is closed, close it if it is open. Returns whether anything changed.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-accordion for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split (the old detail from the element's adapter), host-attribute (no shim).

rows.note: the detail {id, open, source, section} is data only, so both names carry the same object
rows.summary: A section opened or closed, by the person (source user) or by a method (source method). In single mode the section it closed sends its own, after the one asked for, as a native <details name> group does.

x-summary: Sections that open and close, built from data -- a record's groups, a settings panel, an FAQ -- or from <details> in the markup, drawn as the class accordion: the same sizes on the control ladder, appearances, marker and single section. single keeps one open; the headers are buttons with the WAI-ARIA accordion keyboard.
x-renamed: events.sf-accordion:toggle → toggle: the DOM name is sf-accordion-toggle (§8, §16 item 6), the colon name a dated same-detail alias
settings.heading-level: a string holding a numeral → number, integer 2–6 (§16 item 29)
x-decisions: version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, a minor while sf-accordion:toggle holds a dated alias (§4.10).

events: sf-accordion:toggle → sf-accordion-toggle by the alias table (§8, §16 item 6); its detail {id, open, source, section} holds data only, so the row is same-detail: one dispatch, the new name first, one shared detail.

toggle reports both a person (source user) and a call (source method), as before: it is the section's fact, not `change`, so §8's rule that `change` reports a person alone does not remove the method's report.
actions: open, close and toggle {id} answer an outcome (applied; refused unknown, static, disabled or already) instead of true/false (§4.4).

x-target: `expanded` is taken as a read-only value (the open ids, as openIds); `sections` is not added -- items is the list, and §7.2.3 binds a container's `settings.items` -- and `expand` is not added: open does it, and vocabulary §5 expand is the verb that asks a host for children.

a11y-role: none on the host; each header is a native button inside role=heading (aria-level from heading-level), each open panel a region labelled by its header while there are at most six (WAI-ARIA accordion pattern). a11y-name: none on the host -- each header is named by its section's title.

key-effects: on a header Enter and Space toggle its section (toggle:open, the button's own keys), ArrowDown and ArrowUp move to the next and previous enabled header, Home and End to the first and last; Tab reaches each enabled header.

opened (§7.2.1): a closed section's panel carries `hidden` and an open one does not, so a part with start opened inside a section starts when its section opens; the panel's content is the page's live nodes (a slot or the <details>), never copied.

instance ids (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41): the header and panel ids came from a module counter (sf-smart-accordion-<n>); they are the host's path id and a local name now, <path>--trigger-<n> and <path>--panel-<n>; the <details> slots are named locally.
item-shape: items name their fields with `of` (id, title, content, slot, open, disabled, icon, badge); content is text, markup comes through a slot.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json plus <details> in the markup, plus-minus markers and one plain section; probe.json drives the arrows, Home, End, Enter, Space and Tab (gate 16).
css-variables: the eight public variables the sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

$comment: sf-accordion loads on demand like any other Smart element. It draws the
class accordion's markup, so the class accordion is what it draws with: its
sheet (and its runtime, which leaves the element's sections alone), the
icon font for the marker and an icon before a title, and sf-badge, only
when a section carries a badge.

id.description: The section's name in open(id), close(id), toggle(id) and the event; its place (section-1, section-2…) without it. One id names one section: a repeated one is left out.

content.description: The section's text. Text, never markup: markup goes in a slot.

slot.description: The name of a light-DOM slot holding the section's markup; it replaces content.

open.description: Open at first. In single mode only the first open section stays open.

disabled.description: Neither opened nor closed by the person: the header is a disabled button, out of the tab order.

icon.description: An icon before the title, a name from the icon font.

badge.description: A count or a label after the title, drawn by sf-badge.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-accordion for sections that open and close and come from data -- a record's groups of fields, a settings panel, an FAQ -- or are written as <details> in the markup.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not put markup in content: it is shown as text; use a slot
Do not use it to switch between views of one thing: that is sf-tabs
Do not restyle its sections: they are the class accordion's, set its public variables

accessibility.focus: Each header is a native button inside a heading (role heading, aria-level), with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter and Space open and close it. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between the headers and wrap, Home and End go to the first and the last; a disabled header is a disabled button, passed over and out of the tab order. Each panel is a region named by its header while there are six sections or fewer. The single section is a plain heading with nothing in the tab order.

sf-accordion:toggle.summary: A section opened or closed, by the person (source user) or by a method (source method). In single mode the section it closed sends its own, after the one asked for, as a native <details name> group does.

section.description: The section as the element draws it.

isOpen.summary: Whether the section with this id is open. The single section always is.

content.description: The section's text. Text, never markup: markup goes in a slot.

slot.description: The name of a light-DOM slot holding the section's markup; it replaces content.

open.description: Open at first. In single mode only the first open section stays open.

disabled.description: Neither opened nor closed by the person: the header is a disabled button, out of the tab order.

icon.description: An icon before the title, a name from the icon font.

badge.description: A count or a label after the title, drawn by sf-badge.
